symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: Known Hölder smoothness exponent \(\beta\).

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: Local-polynomial order \(\ell=\lfloor\beta\rfloor\), with \(\ell=\beta-1\) when \(\beta\) is an integer.

symbols.name: c_plus

symbols.name: p_min

symbols.name: delta_bar
symbols.def: Fixed upper envelope \(\bar\delta\) for the threshold sequence.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Prespecified noncoverage probability \(\alpha\).

symbols.name: delta_n
symbols.def: Arbitrary deterministic threshold \(\delta_n\) at sample size \(n\).

symbols.name: X

symbols.name: A

symbols.name: O

symbols.name: O_i
symbols.def: The \(i\)-th unit in the sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Law \(P\) of one observed unit.

symbols.name: p_x
symbols.def: Stratum mass \(p_x=P(X=x)\).

symbols.name: pi_x
symbols.def: Borel function \(\pi_x\) whose defining conditional-density identity is imposed by \(\text{ass:conditional-density-law}\).

symbols.name: mu_x_P
symbols.def: The unique continuous function \(\mu_x^P\) that equals an almost-everywhere version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) and satisfies the declared Taylor-remainder Hölder condition.

symbols.name: d_delta
symbols.def: Lower-threshold clamp \(d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\}\).

symbols.name: q_x
symbols.def: Conditional atom mass \(q_x(\delta)=\int_0^\delta\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da=P(A\leq\delta\mid X=x)\).

symbols.name: nu_delta
symbols.def: Observable retained-natural-course contribution \(\nu_\delta(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}]\).

symbols.name: theta_delta
symbols.def: Observed-data target \(\theta_\delta(P)=\nu_\delta(P)+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta)\).

symbols.name: mathcal_M
symbols.def: Finite-stratum Hölder and polynomial-thinning model \(\mathcal M\).

symbols.name: h_n
symbols.def: Bandwidth \(h_n\) defined by the first crossing of the polynomial information balance.

symbols.name: r_n
symbols.def: Candidate frontier \(r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\).

symbols.name: delta_crit
symbols.def: Critical scale \(\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}=n^{-1/[2(\beta\kappa+2\beta+\kappa+1)]}\).

symbols.name: delta_edge
symbols.def: Moving-point boundary scale \(\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}=n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\).

symbols.name: v_ell
symbols.def: Monomial vector \(v_\ell(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^\ell)^\top\).

symbols.name: M_kappa_rho
symbols.def: Normalized reference moment matrix \(M_{\kappa,\rho}=\{\int_0^1v_\ell(u)v_\ell(u)^\top(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du\}/\{\int_0^1(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du\}\) for \(\rho\in[0,\infty)\).

symbols.name: lambda_star
symbols.def: Uniform population-Gram constant \(\lambda_\star=(c_-/c_+)\inf_{\rho\geq0}\lambda_{\min}(M_{\kappa,\rho})\).

symbols.name: I_0
symbols.def: First deterministic sample block satisfying \(|I_0|\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), for the retained natural-course mean.

symbols.name: I_1
symbols.def: Second deterministic sample block satisfying \(|I_1|\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), for atom masses.

symbols.name: I_2
symbols.def: Third deterministic sample block satisfying \(|I_2|\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), for local regressions.

symbols.name: N_x
symbols.def: Local count \(N_x=\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\delta_n\leq A_i\leq\delta_n+h_n\}\).

symbols.name: G_x
symbols.def: Unnormalized local Gram matrix \(G_x=\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,0\leq U_i\leq1\}v_\ell(U_i)v_\ell(U_i)^\top\), where \(U_i=(A_i-\delta_n)/h_n\).

symbols.name: Omega_x
symbols.def: Realized-design event \(\Omega_x=\{N_x>0,\lambda_{\min}(G_x)\geq\lambda_\star N_x/2\}\).

symbols.name: w_ix
symbols.def: Intercept weight \(w_{ix}=\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,0\leq U_i\leq1\}e_0^\top G_x^{-1}v_\ell(U_i)\) on \(\Omega_x\), and \(w_{ix}=0\) off \(\Omega_x\).

symbols.name: theta_hat_n
symbols.def: Sample-split, total-Gram-stabilized estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) of \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\).

symbols.name: CI_n
symbols.def: Bias-aware confidence interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) with a local atom fallback on singular-Gram events.

symbols.name: R_n_star
symbols.def: Minimax absolute-error risk \(R_n^\star=\inf_{\widehat\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)|\).

symbols.name: L_n_star
symbols.def: Minimax worst-case expected length \(L_n^\star=\inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C_n\}\geq1-\alpha}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{len}(C_n)]\).

symbols.name: mathcal_U
symbols.def: Generic notation for the law-specific standard Borel latent-response carrier \(\mathcal U\), bound separately inside each full-data law package.

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: Within one full-data law package, the latent response variable \(U\) taking values in that member's carrier \(\mathcal U\).

symbols.name: g_x
symbols.def: Within one full-data law package and for each \(x\in\mathcal X\), the jointly Borel measurable structural response map \(g_x(a,u)\) on that member's carrier.

symbols.name: Y_a
symbols.def: Within one full-data law package, the potential-outcome process \(a\mapsto Y(a)\), represented simultaneously outside one null set by \(Y(a)=g_X(a,U)\) under \(\text{ass:consistency}\).

symbols.name: P_full
symbols.def: A full-data law package \(P^{\mathrm F}\) that contains its own standard Borel latent carrier, latent variable, response maps, and potential-outcome process together with a probability law whose observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin is \(P\).

symbols.name: psi_delta
symbols.def: Full-data clamp-policy mean \(\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y\{d_\delta(A)\}]\).

symbols.name: m_x_F
symbols.def: For a fixed full-data law package, the fiberwise response mean \(m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[g_x(a,U)\mid X=x]\), computed using that member's carrier and law.

symbols.name: mathcal_M_F
symbols.def: Carrier-heterogeneous full-data structural law-package class \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\).

symbols.name: R_n_F_star
symbols.def: Observed-sample minimax absolute-error risk \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) for the causal clamp mean over \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\).

symbols.name: L_n_F_star
symbols.def: Minimax worst-case expected length \(L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) among observed-sample intervals honest for the causal clamp mean over \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\).

symbols.name: mathcal_M_cont
symbols.def: Finite-stratum polynomial-thinning model \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) with qualitative conditional-regression continuity and no common modulus.

symbols.name: mu_x_cont_P
symbols.def: For \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\), the unique continuous extension \(\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P\) of an almost-everywhere version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) on \([0,\bar\delta]\).

symbols.name: theta_delta_cont
symbols.def: Observed-data clamp target \(\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\) on \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\).

symbols.name: s_n
symbols.def: Continuity-only frontier \(s_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}\).

symbols.name: theta_hat_cont_n
symbols.def: Fixed atom-regression fallback estimator \(\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\).

symbols.name: CI_cont_n
symbols.def: Hoeffding interval \(\mathrm{CI}_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\) using the fixed atom fallback.

symbols.name: R_n_cont_star
symbols.def: Minimax absolute-error risk \(R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\) for \(\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}\) over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\).

symbols.def: Minimax uniformly honest expected length \(L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\) over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\).

symbols.def: Carrier-heterogeneous continuity-only full-data class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\).

symbols.name: R_n_cont_F_star
symbols.def: Observed-sample minimax risk \(R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star\) for the causal clamp mean over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\).

symbols.name: exactHolderBias
symbols.def: For a realized design \(z\), stratum \(x\), and admissible affine weights \(w\), \(\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)\) is the supremum of the absolute intercept error over the declared \([0,1]\)-valued Hölder class.

symbols.name: realizedExactModulus
symbols.def: The quantity \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\) is the infimum of exact Hölder bias plus \(t\) times the \(\ell_2\)-norm of admissible affine weights, totalized to zero when no such weight exists.

symbols.name: exactModulusHandle
symbols.def: The quantity \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t)\) is the real-valued integral of \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\) under the \(n\)-fold iid observed-design law induced by \(P\).

symbols.name: worstExactModulus
symbols.def: The quantity \(\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t)\) is the supremum of the integrated exact-modulus radius over \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\).

symbols.name: t_alpha
symbols.def: The open-question calibration is \(t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}\).

assumptions.condition: The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed from \(P\).
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\), \(P(A\in B\mid X=x)=\int_B\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\).

standard.name: Conditional absolute continuity for a continuous treatment

assumptions.condition: Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), the latent variable \(U\) is \(\mathcal U\)-valued and, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1]\) is jointly Borel measurable, with one \(P^{\mathrm F}\)-null set outside which \(Y(a)=g_X(a,U)\) for every \(a\in[0,1]\) and \(Y=g_X(A,U)\).
Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), \(A\) and \(U\) are conditionally independent given \(X\).
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and Lebesgue-almost every \(a\in[0,1]\), \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\).

novel.justification: The global two-sided measurable envelope is an explicit treatment-assignment design class. It contains beta-type assignment densities proportional to \(a^\kappa\) and their normalized bounded measurable tilts, representing protocols that suppress doses near a contraindicated boundary while permitting irregular assignment elsewhere. It is not asserted to follow from Gaiffas's regular-variation condition.

assumptions.condition: For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), an almost-everywhere version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) has a continuous extension \(\mu_x^P\) satisfying \(\left|\mu_x^P(t)-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}(\mu_x^P)^{(j)}(s)(t-s)^j/j!\right|\leq L|t-s|^\beta\) for all \(s,t\in[0,1]\).

standard.name: Taylor-remainder formulation of Hölder outcome-regression smoothness

assumptions.condition: Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the function \(a\mapsto m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\) is continuous on \([0,\bar\delta]\).

novel.justification: This author-imposed scientific mean-regularity premise is weaker than conditional \(L^1\)-continuity of the full response path: it constrains only the fiberwise structural mean and only on the declared threshold range.  It is not attributed to Díaz et al.

definitions.name: Finite-stratum clamp model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1]):P\text{ satisfies the conditional-density, stratum-mass, polynomial-thinning, and Hölder member conditions}\}\).

definitions.name: Information-balance bandwidth
definitions.construction: \(h_n=\inf\{h\in(0,1-\bar\delta]:n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h)^\kappa\geq1\}\), with \(h_n=1-\bar\delta\) if the set is empty.

definitions.name: Total-Gram-stabilized local-polynomial estimator
definitions.construction: Split the sample into \(I_0,I_1,I_2\). Set \(\widehat\nu_n=|I_0|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\}\), \(\widehat b_x=|I_1|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i\leq\delta_n\}\), and \(\widetilde\mu_x=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}Y_i)\) on \(\Omega_x\), with \(\widetilde\mu_x=1/2\) off \(\Omega_x\). Define \(\widehat\theta_n=\Pi_{[0,1]}[\widehat\nu_n+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x\widetilde\mu_x]\).

definitions.name: Bias-aware atom-fallback interval
definitions.construction: Let \(t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}\), \(b_0=t_\alpha/\sqrt{|I_0|}\), and \(b_1=t_\alpha/\sqrt{|I_1|}\). For each \(x\), set \(B_x=Lh_n^\beta\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|+t_\alpha(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2)^{1/2}\) and \(D_x=(\widehat b_x+b_1)B_x+b_1\) on \(\Omega_x\), while \(D_x=\widehat b_x+b_1\) off \(\Omega_x\). Define \(\mathrm{CI}_n=[\widehat\theta_n-b_0-\sum_xD_x,\widehat\theta_n+b_0+\sum_xD_x]\cap[0,1]\).

definitions.name: Realized-design exact-modulus handle
definitions.construction:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), a split block \(I_2\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\ell\), \(\beta\), \(\kappa\), \(L\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), \(p_{\min}\), \(\delta_n\), \(h_n>0\), and a test multiplier \(t\geq0\).  For a realized design \(z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), put \(u_i=(A_i-\delta_n)/h_n\), \(S_{z,x}=\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ 0\leq u_i\leq1\}\), and
\[
\mathcal W_{z,x}=\left\{w=(w_i)_{i\in I_2}\in\mathbb R^{I_2}: w_i=0\ \text{for }i\notin S_{z,x},\quad \sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell\right\}.
\]
If \(V_{z,x}\) is the matrix whose row indexed by \(i\in S_{z,x}\) is \(v_\ell(u_i)^\top\), these are equivalently the affine realized-design constraints \(V_{z,x}^\top w_{S_{z,x}}=e_0\), and the associated total Gram is \(G_x=V_{z,x}^\top V_{z,x}\).  Let \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\) be the class of functions \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) that are continuous and satisfy
\[
\left|f(a')-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}f^{(j)}(a)(a'-a)^j/j!\right|\leq L|a'-a|^\beta
\quad\text{for every }a,a'\in[0,1],
\]
where the derivatives are the intrinsic derivatives on \([0,1]\) used in the declared Hölder condition.  For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), define the exact realized Hölder bias and conditional radius objective by
\[
\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)
=\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{\beta,L}}
\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i f(A_i)-f(\delta_n)\right|,
\qquad
\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w)
=\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)+t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The realized exact modulus is the real-valued totalization
\[
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)=
\begin{cases}
\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}}\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w),&\mathcal W_{z,x}\neq\varnothing,\\
0,&\mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus the empty affine-feasible set has value zero, matching the real \(\operatorname{sInf}\) convention in the verified construction.  Define
\[
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t)
=\int \operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\,
\mathrm d(P_{X,A}^{\otimes n})(z),
\]
the real-valued integral under the \(n\)-fold independent observed-design law induced by \(P\).  The inputs \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min}\) enter by requiring that \(P\) satisfy the corresponding member conditions of \(\mathcal M\); they do not impose any additional smoothness on \(\pi_x\).  Finally set
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2},\qquad
\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)
=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t_\alpha).
\]
Both \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\) and \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\) are radius, or half-length, quantities.  An untruncated symmetric interval with such radius has full length twice the radius.  The zero value on \(\mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing\) only totalizes this candidate handle on singular designs; no validity, nondegeneracy, honesty, or optimality of an interval using that convention is asserted here.

definitions.name: Structural full-data clamp model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) is the collection of full-data law packages \(P^{\mathrm F}\) with the following memberwise structure.  Each member carries its own standard Borel latent-response space \(\mathcal U\), an \(\mathcal U\)-valued random variable \(U\), jointly Borel maps \(g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1]\) for \(x\in\mathcal X\), and a jointly measurable process \(\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}\), together with a probability law for \((X,A,Y,U,\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\})\).  Its \((X,A,Y)\)-margin is some \(P\in\mathcal M\), and, within that member's own carrier, the simultaneous latent-response consistency, latent randomization, and fiberwise structural-mean continuity on \([0,\bar\delta]\) member conditions hold.  Different members may use different standard Borel carriers; no common carrier and no carrier-richness condition is imposed.

definitions.name: Causal minimax risk and honest expected length
Continuity-only finite-stratum clamp model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) is the set of laws \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])\) satisfying \(\texttt{ass:conditional-density-law}\), \(\texttt{ass:stratum-mass}\), and \(\texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning}\), and such that, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), an almost-everywhere version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) admits a continuous extension to \([0,\bar\delta]\).  There is no common Hölder exponent, modulus, or radius.

definitions.name: Continuity-only fixed atom fallback estimator
definitions.construction:
Using the deterministic split blocks \(I_0,I_1\), put
\[
 \widehat\nu_n=|I_0|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\},
 \qquad
 \widehat b_x=|I_1|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i\leq\delta_n\},
\]
and define the fixed-regression-fallback estimator
\[
 \widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}
 =\Pi_{[0,1]}\left\{\widehat\nu_n+\frac12\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x\right\}.
\]
It uses no local regression and no propensity estimate.

definitions.name: Continuity-only Hoeffding interval
definitions.construction:
Let
\[
 t_{j,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2|I_j|}}
 \quad(j=0,1),
 \qquad \widehat B_n=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x.
\]
Define the Hoeffding interval
\[
 \mathrm{CI}_{n,\mathrm{cont}}
 =\left[
 \widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}-t_{0,\alpha}-t_{1,\alpha}-\frac12\widehat B_n,
 \widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}+t_{0,\alpha}+t_{1,\alpha}+\frac12\widehat B_n
 \right]\cap[0,1].
\]

definitions.name: Continuity-only structural full-data clamp model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) is the collection of full-data law packages having the memberwise carrier, latent variable, jointly Borel response maps, and jointly measurable potential-outcome process described in \(\texttt{def:full-data-model-class}\), whose observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\), and which satisfy \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\), \(\texttt{ass:exchangeability}\), and \(\texttt{ass:full-data-response-continuity}\).  As before, carriers may vary across members.

definitions.name: Continuity-only observed and causal decision criteria
definitions.construction:
For estimators and intervals measurable with respect to \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), define
\[
 R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star
 =\inf_{\widehat\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}|\widehat\theta-\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)|
\]
and
\[
 L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star
 =\inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}P^{\otimes n}
 \{\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\in C_n\}\geq1-\alpha}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{len}(C_n)].
\]
For the full-data class define
\[
 R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
 =\inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
 \mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}|\widehat\psi-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})|
\]
and
\[
 L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
 =\inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
 (P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in C_n\}\geq1-\alpha}
 \sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
 \mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{len}(C_n)].
\]

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), the conditional pushforward law satisfies \(P\{d_\delta(A)\in\mathrm da\mid X=x\}=\pi_x(a)\mathbf 1\{a>\delta\}\,\mathrm da+q_x(\delta)\,\delta_\delta(\mathrm da)\), with \(c_-\delta^{\kappa+1}/(\kappa+1)\leq q_x(\delta)\leq c_+\delta^{\kappa+1}/(\kappa+1)\).
statements.justification: This cited setup specializes the threshold-LMTP pushforward calculation to the deterministic clamp and fixes the mixed dominating measure used to interpret the observed functional.
statements.gap: Díaz et al. supply threshold-LMTP identification, and McCoy et al. formulate clipped MTP ratios with an appropriate mixed dominating measure; this proposition claims no novelty beyond recording their specialization in the notation of the statistical frontier.
statements.consumer: The formula connects the observed-data target to the user-specified lower-threshold policy in the \(\texttt{lmtp}\) workflow.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\).  For every Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\), Definition \texttt{def:clamp-policy} gives the disjoint inverse-image decomposition
\[
 \{d_\delta(A)\in B\}
 =\{A\in B\cap(\delta,1]\}
   \mathbin{\dot\cup}
   \bigl(\{A\in[0,\delta]\}\cap\{\delta\in B\}\bigr).
\]
By Assumption \texttt{ass:conditional-density-law}, conditional on \(X=x\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P\{d_\delta(A)\in B\mid X=x\}
 &=\int_{B\cap(\delta,1]}\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da
   +\mathbf 1\{\delta\in B\}\int_0^\delta\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\\
 &=\int_B\pi_x(a)\mathbf 1\{a>\delta\}\,\mathrm da
   +q_x(\delta)\delta_\delta(B),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the last equality is the definition of \(q_x\).  Equality on every Borel set proves the asserted equality of measures.  Finally, Assumption \texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning} and integration of its almost-everywhere inequalities give
\[
 \frac{c_-}{\kappa+1}\delta^{\kappa+1}
 =\int_0^\delta c_-a^\kappa\,\mathrm da
 \le q_x(\delta)
 \le\int_0^\delta c_+a^\kappa\,\mathrm da
 =\frac{c_+}{\kappa+1}\delta^{\kappa+1}.
\]
This also covers \(\delta=0\), when all three quantities vanish.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), \(d_\delta(A)\) lies in the support of the conditional natural-treatment law given \(X=x\) almost surely. At \(\delta=0\) this follows from the identity map; at \(\delta>0\) every neighborhood of \(\delta\) has positive conditional probability by conditional absolute continuity and the lower polynomial envelope.
statements.justification: The support statement records why no separate pointwise density-positivity assumption is needed for causal interpretation of the clamp.
statements.gap: This is the standard modified-policy support requirement specialized to a boundary-thinned continuous treatment law, not a novel statistical claim.
statements.consumer: The proposition discharges the positivity premise in the causal bridge while keeping causal assumptions outside the minimax model.
statements.proof_tex:
For a probability measure on \([0,1]\), call \(a\) a support point when every relatively open neighborhood of \(a\) has positive probability.  Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\).  If \(V\) is any relatively open neighborhood of any \(a\in[0,1]\), then \(V\) contains a nondegenerate interval \(I\subseteq[0,1]\).  Assumptions \texttt{ass:conditional-density-law} and \texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning} imply
\[
 P(A\in V\mid X=x)
 \geq \int_I\pi_x(t)\,\mathrm dt
 \geq c_-\int_I t^\kappa\,\mathrm dt>0.
\]
The last strict inequality holds also when the closure of \(I\) meets zero, because \(t^\kappa>0\) for every \(t>0\).  Thus the conditional natural-treatment support is all of \([0,1]\).  Definition \texttt{def:clamp-policy} gives \(d_\delta(A)\in[0,1]\) almost surely, so \(d_\delta(A)\) belongs to that support almost surely.  In particular, at \(\delta=0\) the map is the identity; when \(\delta>0\), the preceding display applied to every neighborhood of \(\delta\) verifies the claimed boundary support directly.

statements.statement: Let \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\), let \(P\in\mathcal M\) be its observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin, and interpret \(\mathcal U\), \(U\), \(g_x\), and \(\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}\) as the carrier components packaged by this member.  Define \(m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[g_x(a,U)\mid X=x]\).  Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and Borel \(B\subseteq[0,1]\), \(\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y\mathbf 1\{A\in B\}\mid X=x]=\int_Bm_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\), and \(m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mu_x^P(a)\) for every \(a\in[0,\bar\delta]\).  Consequently, for every \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), \(d_\delta(A)\) belongs to the support of the conditional natural-treatment law almost surely, \(Y\{d_\delta(A)\}=Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}+Y(\delta)\mathbf 1\{A\leq\delta\}\) almost surely, and \(\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}]+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta)=\theta_\delta(P)\).
statements.justification: This proposition derives the exact deterministic clamp-policy equality fiberwise for the carrier packaged by each full-data law, transporting the observed identifying functional to the causal target without assuming pointwise mean/version equality.
statements.gap: Díaz et al. supply the LMTP structural template and support logic, but not the fiberwise structural-mean continuity on \([0,\bar\delta]\) used here to extend almost-everywhere regression equality pointwise over the threshold range; the carrier is quantified internally to each law.
statements.consumer: The causal-frontier lift uses this fiberwise bridge for the exact unsmoothed causal clamp mean; the result targets the same lower-threshold policy specification as the official \(\texttt{lmtp}\) workflow and motivates a future atom-aware implementation.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\), and let \(P\in\mathcal M\) be its observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin.  Definition \(\texttt{def:full-data-model-class}\) supplies, for this member, a standard Borel carrier \(\mathcal U\), an \(\mathcal U\)-valued variable \(U\), jointly Borel maps \(g_x\), and a jointly measurable process \(Y(a)\); it also imposes Assumptions \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\), \(\texttt{ass:exchangeability}\), and \(\texttt{ass:full-data-response-continuity}\).  Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:stratum-mass}\) gives
\[
 P^{\mathrm F}(X=x)=P(X=x)=p_x\geq p_{\min}>0,
 \tag{1}
\]
so conditioning on \(X=x\) is well defined.

Assumption \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\) gives one \(P^{\mathrm F}\)-probability-one event on which, simultaneously for every \(a\in[0,1]\),
\[
 Y(a)=g_X(a,U),
 \qquad
 Y=g_X(A,U).
 \tag{2}
\]
By Assumption \(\texttt{ass:exchangeability}\), \(A\) and \(U\) are conditionally independent given \(X\).  Therefore, on the positive-probability stratum in (1),
\[
 P^{\mathrm F}_{(A,U)\mid X=x}
 =P^{\mathrm F}_{A\mid X=x}\otimes P^{\mathrm F}_{U\mid X=x}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Define, as in the proposition,
\[
 m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)
 =\int_{\mathcal U}g_x(a,u)\,P^{\mathrm F}(\mathrm du\mid X=x).
 \tag{4}
\]
The integrand in (4) is jointly Borel and bounded in \([0,1]\) by Definition \(\texttt{def:full-data-model-class}\).  Hence its parameter integral is Borel, and the defining iterated-integral identity for the product probability in (3) applies to the nonnegative integrals below.  For every Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\), equations (2)--(4), followed by Assumption \(\texttt{ass:conditional-density-law}\), yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y\mathbf 1\{A\in B\}\mid X=x]
 &=\int_{B\times\mathcal U}g_x(a,u)\,
   \{P^{\mathrm F}_{A\mid X=x}\otimes P^{\mathrm F}_{U\mid X=x}\}
   (\mathrm da,\mathrm du)\\
 &=\int_Bm_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\,P^{\mathrm F}(\mathrm da\mid X=x)\\
 &=\int_Bm_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
This proves the conditional integral identity.

We next derive, rather than assume, the pointwise equality needed at a threshold.  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:holder-regression}\) says that \(\mu_x^P\) is continuous on \([0,1]\) and is an almost-everywhere version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\).  Together with Assumption \(\texttt{ass:conditional-density-law}\), this gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A\in B\}\mid X=x]
 =\int_B\mu_x^P(a)\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da
 \tag{6}
\]
for every Borel \(B\subseteq[0,1]\).  Since \(P\) is the observed margin of \(P^{\mathrm F}\), equations (5)--(6) imply
\[
 \int_B\{m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)-\mu_x^P(a)\}\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da=0
 \quad\text{for every Borel }B\subseteq[0,1].
 \tag{7}
\]
Put \(f_x=m_x^{\mathrm F}-\mu_x^P\).  For every integer \(j\geq1\), apply (7) to the Borel sets \(B_j^+=\{a:f_x(a)\geq1/j\}\) and \(B_j^-=\{a:f_x(a)\leq-1/j\}\).  Then
\[
 0=\int_{B_j^+}f_x(a)\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da
 \geq \frac1j\int_{B_j^+}\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da,
 \qquad
 0=\int_{B_j^-}f_x(a)\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da
 \leq-\frac1j\int_{B_j^-}\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da.
 \tag{8}
\]
Thus \(f_x=0\) for \(\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\)-almost every \(a\).  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning}\), together with \(c_->0\) and \(\kappa\geq0\), gives
\[
 \pi_x(a)\geq c_-a^\kappa>0
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }a\in(0,1].
 \tag{9}
\]
Consequently \(f_x=0\) Lebesgue-almost everywhere on \((0,\bar\delta]\).  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:full-data-response-continuity}\) makes \(m_x^{\mathrm F}\) continuous on \([0,\bar\delta]\), while Assumption \(\texttt{ass:holder-regression}\) makes \(\mu_x^P\) continuous there.  If \(f_x(a_0)\neq0\) at some \(a_0\in[0,\bar\delta]\), relative continuity would produce a relative neighborhood of \(a_0\) on which \(|f_x|\) is bounded away from zero.  Since \(\bar\delta>0\), that neighborhood intersects \((0,\bar\delta]\) in a set of positive Lebesgue measure, contradicting the preceding almost-everywhere equality.  Hence
\[
 m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mu_x^P(a)
 \quad\text{for every }a\in[0,\bar\delta].
 \tag{10}
\]
In particular, equality at \(a=0\) follows by continuity from punctured right neighborhoods; it is not imposed through a choice of conditional-expectation version.

Fix \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\).  Definition \(\texttt{def:clamp-policy}\) and the simultaneous identities (2) imply, on the same probability-one event,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Y\{d_\delta(A)\}
 &=g_X\{\max(A,\delta),U\}\\
 &=g_X(A,U)\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}
   +g_X(\delta,U)\mathbf 1\{A\leq\delta\}\\
 &=Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}+Y(\delta)\mathbf 1\{A\leq\delta\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
This equality also covers \(A=\delta\), because (2) then gives \(Y=Y(\delta)\).  Conditional independence in (3), equations (2), (4), and (10), and Proposition \(\texttt{prop:pushforward-setup}\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(\delta)\mathbf 1\{A\leq\delta\}\mid X=x]
 &=m_x^{\mathrm F}(\delta)P^{\mathrm F}(A\leq\delta\mid X=x)\\
 &=\mu_x^P(\delta)\int_0^\delta\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\\
 &=\mu_x^P(\delta)q_x(\delta).
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
Taking expectations in (11), substituting (12), using equality of observed margins for the retained-natural-course term, and summing over the finite set \(\mathcal X\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
 &=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y\{d_\delta(A)\}]\\
 &=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}]
   +\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta)\\
 &=\theta_\delta(P).
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
The first and last equalities in (13) are the definitions of \(\psi_\delta\) and \(\theta_\delta\).  Proposition \(\texttt{prop:policy-support}\) supplies the support assertion throughout \([0,\bar\delta]\).  At \(\delta=0\), Assumption \(\texttt{ass:conditional-density-law}\) gives \(q_x(0)=0\) and the clamp is the identity; at \(\delta=\bar\delta<1\), equation (10) remains valid.  This proves every asserted conclusion on the full closed threshold range.

statements.statement: Uniformly over deterministic \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\), the bandwidth satisfies \(n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa\asymp1\) and the effective local count satisfies \(n h_n(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa\asymp h_n^{-2\beta}\). If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}\to\infty\), then \(h_n\asymp(n\delta_n^\kappa)^{-1/(2\beta+1)}\); if \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}=O(1)\), then \(h_n\asymp n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\).
statements.justification: This balance converts polynomial thinning into the information scale that drives both estimation and inference.
statements.gap: Gaiffas derives the balance at a fixed degenerate point; the clamp requires a moving point \(\delta_n\) and an atom multiplier that changes the relevant phase boundary.
statements.consumer: The local-count identity is the normalization needed by the total-Gram probability bound and by bandwidth selection in the threshold-policy estimator.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(H=1-\bar\delta>0\) and
\[
 F_{n,\delta}(h)=n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta+h)^\kappa,
 \qquad 0<h\leq H.
\]
The restrictions \(\beta>0\) and \(\kappa\geq0\) make this function continuous and strictly increasing.  Moreover,
\[
 F_{n,\delta}(H)\geq nH^{2\beta+\kappa+1},
\]
uniformly in \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\).  Hence, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the set in Definition \texttt{def:bandwidth} is nonempty and its infimum is the unique solution of
\[
 n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa=1. \tag{1}
\]
This proves the first asserted comparison, in fact with equality for all such \(n\).  Dividing (1) by \(h_n^{2\beta}\) gives
\[
 n h_n(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa=h_n^{-2\beta}, \tag{2}
\]
which proves the effective-count assertion.

Let \(e_n=\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}=n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\).  If \(\delta_n/e_n\to\infty\), set \(z_n=h_n/\delta_n\).  Equation (1) becomes
\[
 n\delta_n^{2\beta+\kappa+1}z_n^{2\beta+1}(1+z_n)^\kappa=1.
\]
Its first factor tends to infinity, so monotonicity forces \(z_n\to0\).  Substitution back into (1) yields
\[
 h_n^{2\beta+1}\sim(n\delta_n^\kappa)^{-1},
 \qquad
 h_n\asymp(n\delta_n^\kappa)^{-1/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
If instead \(d_n=\delta_n/e_n=O(1)\) and \(s_n=h_n/e_n\), then (1) is
\[
 s_n^{2\beta+1}(d_n+s_n)^\kappa=1. \tag{3}
\]
Because \(d_n\) is bounded, (3) bounds \(s_n\) above and away from zero by constants depending only on that bound and the declared exponents.  Thus \(h_n\asymp e_n=n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\), as claimed.  Every comparison was uniform in the deterministic threshold within its stated regime.

statements.statement: The constant \(\lambda_\star\) is strictly positive. There are constants \(C,c>0\), depending only on the declared model constants, such that uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and deterministic \(\delta_n\), \(P(\Omega_x^c)\leq C\exp\{-c n h_n(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa\}\). On \(\Omega_x\), the exact intercept weights reproduce polynomials through degree \(\ell\) and obey \(\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|\leq C\) and \(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2\leq C/N_x\). No continuity or differentiability of \(\pi_x\) beyond two-sided polynomial comparability is required.
statements.justification: This is the early-kill lemma: it makes the singular-Gram fallback negligible at the atom-weighted target scale under measurable density envelopes alone.
statements.gap: Gaiffas stabilizes local polynomial Gram matrices under an exact regularly varying design; the present claim is uniform over every measurable density between two polynomial envelopes and controls the exact \(\ell_1\)- and \(\ell_2\)-weight norms.
statements.consumer: The lemma is the sole random-design input needed for the finite-sample honest interval and prevents an undocumented propensity-smoothness condition from entering the official workflow.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(d=\ell+1\), \(m=|I_2|\), \(\delta=\delta_n\), and \(h=h_n\).  First consider the reference matrices.  For every nonzero \(z\in\mathbb R^d\), the polynomial \(u\mapsto z^\top v_\ell(u)\) is nonzero except on a finite set.  Consequently,
\[
 z^\top M_{\kappa,\rho}z
 =\frac{\int_0^1\{z^\top v_\ell(u)\}^2(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
        {\int_0^1(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}>0
\]
for every \(\rho\geq0\).  The entries are continuous in \(\rho\), and after dividing numerator and denominator by \(\rho^\kappa\) they converge as \(\rho\to\infty\) to the entries of \(\int_0^1v_\ell(u)v_\ell(u)^\top\,\mathrm du\), another positive-definite matrix.  Continuity of the smallest eigenvalue on the compactification \([0,\infty]\) therefore gives
\[
 \inf_{\rho\geq0}\lambda_{\min}(M_{\kappa,\rho})>0.
\]
Since \(c_->0\) and \(c_+<\infty\), the definition of \(\lambda_\star\) proves \(\lambda_\star>0\).

Let
\[
 s_x=P\{X=x,\delta\leq A\leq\delta+h\},
 \qquad \mu_{N,x}=ms_x.
\]
Assumptions \texttt{ass:stratum-mass}, \texttt{ass:conditional-density-law}, and \texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning} imply
\[
 c_1h(\delta+h)^\kappa\leq s_x\leq c_2h(\delta+h)^\kappa, \tag{4}
\]
where for the lower bound one integrates over \([\delta+h/2,\delta+h]\) and uses \(a^\kappa\geq2^{-\kappa}(\delta+h)^\kappa\).  Since \(m\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), (4) and Lemma \texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases} give
\[
 \mu_{N,x}\asymp nh(\delta+h)^\kappa\asymp h^{-2\beta}. \tag{5}
\]

By Assumption \texttt{ass:iid-sampling}, \(N_x\) is binomial with parameters \(m,s_x\).  Conditional on \(N_x=k>0\), the \(k\) local values \(U=(A-\delta)/h\) are independent with density proportional to \(u\mapsto\pi_x(\delta+hu)\) on \([0,1]\).  Let \(Q_x\) be the conditional second-moment matrix of \(v_\ell(U)\).  For every \(z\in\mathbb R^d\), Assumption \texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning} yields, with \(\rho=\delta/h\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 z^\top Q_xz
 &\geq\frac{c_-\int_0^1\{z^\top v_\ell(u)\}^2(\delta+hu)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
              {c_+\int_0^1(\delta+hu)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}\\
 &=\frac{c_-}{c_+}z^\top M_{\kappa,\rho}z
 \geq\lambda_\star\lVert z\rVert_2^2.
 \end{aligned} \tag{6}
\]
This comparison uses only the two measurable density envelopes.

Each entry of \(v_\ell(U)v_\ell(U)^\top\) lies in \([0,1]\).  Applying the scalar exponential-Markov bound to each centered bounded entry and taking a union bound over the fixed \(d^2\) entries gives
\[
 P\left(\left.\left\|k^{-1}G_x-Q_x\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\lambda_\star/2\,\right|N_x=k\right)
 \leq 2d^2\exp(-c_0k), \tag{7}
\]
because the operator norm is at most \(d\) times the largest absolute entry.  On the complement of the event in (7), (6) implies \(\lambda_{\min}(G_x)\geq k\lambda_\star/2\).  The binomial generating function now gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(\Omega_x^c)
 &\leq C_0\mathbb E[\exp(-c_0N_x)]\\
 &=C_0\{1-s_x+s_xe^{-c_0}\}^{m}
 \leq C_0\exp\{-c_1ms_x\}\\
 &\leq C\exp\{-cnh(\delta+h)^\kappa\},
 \end{aligned} \tag{8}
\]
where (4) was used in the last line.  This includes the event \(N_x=0\).

It remains to verify the exact weight statements.  On \(\Omega_x\), for \(0\leq j\leq\ell\),
\[
 \sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}U_i^j
 =e_0^\top G_x^{-1}\left\{\sum_{i:X_i=x,\,0\leq U_i\leq1}v_\ell(U_i)U_i^j\right\}
 =e_0^\top G_x^{-1}G_xe_j
 =\mathbf 1\{j=0\}. \tag{9}
\]
Furthermore, \(\lVert v_\ell(u)\rVert_2\leq\sqrt d\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\lVert G_x^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2/(\lambda_\star N_x)\), whence
\[
 \sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|
 \leq N_x\frac{2\sqrt d}{\lambda_\star N_x}
 \leq C, \tag{10}
\]
and, using the definition of \(G_x\),
\[
 \sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2
 =e_0^\top G_x^{-1}G_xG_x^{-1}e_0
 =e_0^\top G_x^{-1}e_0
 \leq\frac{2}{\lambda_\star N_x}. \tag{11}
\]
Equations (8)--(11) prove every assertion with constants depending only on the declared model constants.

statements.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the declared model constants, such that for every deterministic threshold sequence and all sufficiently large \(n\), \(c r_n\leq R_n^\star\leq\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_n-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)|\leq C r_n\). The lower bound is the maximum, and therefore the same order as the sum, of a same-class global Bernoulli shift yielding \(n^{-1/2}\) separation and a same-class localized Bernoulli regression perturbation of width \(h_n\) yielding \(\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\) separation with bounded product divergence.
statements.justification: The theorem gives the exact order frontier for the unsmoothed clamp target, including both its regular and point-evaluation components.
statements.gap: Gaiffas establishes an unweighted fixed-point regression rate under a degenerate random design, while Díaz et al. identify the threshold-LMTP mean without a minimax rate; McCoy et al. analyze a stochastic-shift effect-modifier target under high-probability regularity. None gives the matched risk frontier for the observed retained-natural-course mean plus an atom-weighted moving point evaluation.
statements.consumer: An analyst using the lower-threshold \(\texttt{lmtp}\) policy obtains the first threshold-sequence-specific accuracy benchmark without replacing the policy by a stochastic region average.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(\delta=\delta_n\), \(h=h_n\), \(m_j=|I_j|\), and
\[
 b_x=P(X=x,A\leq\delta)=p_xq_x(\delta).
\]
Proposition \texttt{prop:pushforward-setup} gives
\[
 0\leq b_x\leq \frac{c_+}{\kappa+1}\delta^{\kappa+1}. \tag{1}
\]
We first prove the upper bound for the single sample map in Definition \texttt{def:total-gram-estimator}.  Since \(m_0,m_1\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), Assumption \texttt{ass:iid-sampling}, \(0\leq Y\leq1\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(Z)\leq1/4\) for \(0\leq Z\leq1\) imply, by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\nu_n-\nu_\delta(P)|\leq Cn^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat b_x-b_x|\leq Cn^{-1/2}. \tag{2}
\]

On \(\Omega_x\), write \(S_x=\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}Y_i\).  Conditional on \(\mathscr D_2=\sigma\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), Assumption \texttt{ass:iid-sampling} makes the outcomes independent, and the defining version \(\mu_x^P\) is their conditional mean at almost every realized treatment value.  Polynomial reproduction in Lemma \texttt{lem:total-gram} makes the Taylor polynomial of \(\mu_x^P\) about \(\delta\) contribute exactly its intercept.  Assumption \texttt{ass:holder-regression}, boundedness of \(Y\), and the two weight bounds in that lemma therefore give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|\mathbb E_P[S_x\mid\mathscr D_2]-\mu_x^P(\delta)\right|
 &\leq Lh^\beta\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|\leq Ch^\beta,\\
 \operatorname{Var}_P(S_x\mid\mathscr D_2)
 &\leq\frac14\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2\leq\frac{C}{N_x}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{3}
\]
Projection onto \([0,1]\) cannot increase distance from \(\mu_x^P(\delta)\in[0,1]\).

We record the count calculation needed to integrate (3).  The variable \(N_x\) is binomial with mean
\[
 \lambda_x=m_2p_x\int_\delta^{\delta+h}\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da.
\]
Assumptions \texttt{ass:stratum-mass} and \texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning}, together with the subinterval \([\delta+h/2,\delta+h]\), yield
\[
 cnh(\delta+h)^\kappa\leq\lambda_x\leq Cnh(\delta+h)^\kappa. \tag{4}
\]
For a binomial \(N\) of mean \(\lambda=mp\), exponential Markov and \(1+z\leq e^z\) give, at \(t=\log2\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(N<\lambda/2)
 &\leq e^{t\lambda/2}\mathbb E e^{-tN}
 =e^{t\lambda/2}(1-p+pe^{-t})^m\\
 &\leq\exp\{\lambda(t/2+e^{-t}-1)\}
 \leq e^{-\lambda/8}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Splitting according to \(N\geq\lambda/2\) consequently gives
\[
 \mathbb E[N^{-1/2}\mathbf 1\{N>0\}]
 \leq (2/\lambda)^{1/2}+e^{-\lambda/8}
 \leq C\lambda^{-1/2}. \tag{5}
\]
Here and below constants absorb the harmless bounded range of \(\lambda\); by (4) and Lemma \texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases}, \(\lambda_x\asymp h^{-2\beta}\).  On \(\Omega_x^c\), both the fallback and the true regression value lie in \([0,1]\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:total-gram} and \(e^{-ct}\leq C_ct^{-1/2}\) for \(t\geq1\), used with \(t=h^{-2\beta}\), therefore imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widetilde\mu_x-\mu_x^P(\delta)|
 \leq Ch^\beta+C\mathbb E_P[N_x^{-1/2}\mathbf 1\{N_x>0\}]
       +P(\Omega_x^c)
 \leq Ch^\beta. \tag{6}
\]

Before the final projection, add and subtract \(b_x\widetilde\mu_x\), use \(0\leq\widetilde\mu_x\leq1\), and combine (1), (2), and (6):
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_n-\theta_\delta(P)|
 &\leq \mathbb E_P|\widehat\nu_n-\nu_\delta(P)|
 +\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\left\{\mathbb E_P|\widehat b_x-b_x|
 +b_x\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\mu_x-\mu_x^P(\delta)|\right\}\\
 &\leq C\{n^{-1/2}+\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta\}=Cr_n. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]
The displayed inequality survives projection because \(\theta_\delta(P)\in[0,1]\).  The fixed value of \(J\) makes the constant uniform in \(P\), \(x\), and the deterministic threshold sequence.  Taking the supremum proves the claimed minimax upper bound with one data-driven estimator.

For the converse, we construct two pairs inside the same class \(\mathcal M\).  In both, take \(p_x=1/J\) and \(\pi_x(a)=(\kappa+1)a^\kappa\) for every stratum.  These choices satisfy Assumptions \texttt{ass:stratum-mass} and \texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning}, because \(p_{\min}\leq1/J\) and \(c_-\leq\kappa+1\leq c_+\).  For the global pair, let \(Y\mid(A,X)\) be Bernoulli with mean \(1/2\) under \(P_0\) and \(1/2+a_0n^{-1/2}\) under \(P_1\), where \(a_0>0\) is a sufficiently small fixed constant.  Both regressions obey Assumption \texttt{ass:holder-regression}, and the two parts of the definition of \(\theta_\delta\) partition the treatment law.  Hence
\[
 |\theta_\delta(P_1)-\theta_\delta(P_0)|=a_0n^{-1/2}. \tag{8}
\]
The one-observation chi-square divergence is \(4a_0^2/n\), so independence gives
\[
 \chi^2(P_1^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 =(1+4a_0^2/n)^n-1\leq e^{4a_0^2}-1. \tag{9}
\]

For the localized pair, fix a nonnegative smooth bump \(\varphi\) supported on \([-1,1]\) with \(\varphi(0)=1\), for example the normalized function \(u\mapsto\exp\{-1/(1-u^2)\}\mathbf 1\{|u|<1\}\).  Direct Taylor expansion and rescaling give a finite constant \(C_{\varphi,\beta}\) such that \(h^\beta\varphi((\,cdot-\delta)/h)\), restricted to \([0,1]\), satisfies the Taylor-remainder Hölder condition with radius \(C_{\varphi,\beta}\).  Define, in every stratum,
\[
 \mu_0(a)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_1(a)=\frac12+a_1h^\beta\varphi((a-\delta)/h), \tag{10}
\]
where the fixed \(a_1>0\) is small enough that \(a_1C_{\varphi,\beta}\leq L\) and \(a_1\|\varphi\|_\infty\leq1/4\).  Bernoulli outcomes with these conditional means define two further members of \(\mathcal M\).  Since the Bernoulli chi-square divergence from mean \(1/2\) to mean \(1/2+g\) equals \(4g^2\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \chi^2(P_1,P_0)
 &=4a_1^2h^{2\beta}\int_0^1
   \varphi((a-\delta)/h)^2(\kappa+1)a^\kappa\,\mathrm da\\
 &\leq Ca_1^2h^{2\beta+1}(\delta+h)^\kappa.
 \end{aligned} \tag{11}
\]
Definition \texttt{def:bandwidth} and Lemma \texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases} make \(n\) times the last expression at most \(Ca_1^2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Thus
\[
 \chi^2(P_1^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\exp(Ca_1^2)-1. \tag{12}
\]
For this design, \(q_x(\delta)=\delta^{\kappa+1}\).  The perturbation is nonnegative, and its value at the clamp atom is \(a_1h^\beta\).  The retained-natural-course part is also nonnegative, so
\[
 \theta_\delta(P_1)-\theta_\delta(P_0)
 \geq a_1\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta. \tag{13}
\]

For completeness, if \(Q_1\ll Q_0\) has likelihood ratio \(Z\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|Q_1-Q_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\sup_E|\mathbb E_{Q_0}[(Z-1)\mathbf 1_E]|
 \leq\sqrt{\chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)}. \tag{14}
\]
Choose \(a_0,a_1\) so that both product total variations are at most \(1/2\).  For an arbitrary estimator \(T\), a pair with target values \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), and separation \(\Delta\), set \(E=\{|T-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\).  Then
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \max_{j=0,1}\mathbb E_{Q_j}|T-\theta_j|
 &\geq\frac{\Delta}{4}\{Q_0(E^c)+Q_1(E)\}\\
 &\geq\frac{\Delta}{4}\{1-\|Q_1-Q_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}
 \geq\frac{\Delta}{8}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{15}
\]
Apply (15) separately to (8) and (13), then use \(\max(u,v)\geq(u+v)/2\).  This proves
\[
 R_n^\star\geq c\max\{n^{-1/2},\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta\}
 \geq c'\{n^{-1/2}+\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta\}=c'r_n. \tag{16}
\]
Together, (7) and (16) establish every assertion of the theorem, including the announced global-shift and localized-Bernoulli mechanisms.

statements.statement: For every \(n\) large enough, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_n\}\geq1-\alpha\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)]\leq C r_n\). Conversely, every confidence interval with coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M\) satisfies \(L_n^\star\geq c r_n\). The interval adapts the bias-aware construction of Armstrong and Kolesár to the distinct polynomially thinned random-design clamp functional and remains honest on singular-Gram realizations through the atom fallback.
statements.justification: Risk optimality alone does not justify uncertainty quantification for a nonregular target; the confidence-length statement makes honesty a theorem-level deliverable.
statements.gap: Armstrong and Kolesár calibrate smoothing bias for nonparametric regression under fixed-design formulations, Gaiffas does not construct honest intervals, and McCoy et al.'s high-probability regularity theory does not give uniformly honest expected length. None integrates a random singular-Gram event at a shrinking atom-mass scale.
statements.consumer: The interval replaces the invalid Wald output that a continuous threshold policy can otherwise produce in the \(\texttt{lmtp}\) workflow.
statements.proof_tex:
Again put \(\delta=\delta_n\), \(h=h_n\), \(b_x=p_xq_x(\delta)\), and \(m_j=|I_j|\).  Consider the simultaneous events
\[
 \begin{split}
 E_0&=\{|\widehat\nu_n-\nu_\delta(P)|\leq b_0\},\\
 E_{1x}&=\{|\widehat b_x-b_x|\leq b_1\},\\
 E_{2x}&=\Omega_x^c\ \cup\
 \left\{\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}Y_i-\mu_x^P(\delta)\right|\leq B_x\right\}.
 \end{split} \tag{17}
\]
We first derive the concentration inequality used below.  If a centered random variable \(W\) lies in an interval of length \(d\), its cumulant generating function \(K(\lambda)=\log\mathbb E e^{\lambda W}\) satisfies \(K(0)=K'(0)=0\) and
\[
 K''(\lambda)=\operatorname{Var}_{\lambda}(W)\leq d^2/4,
\]
because variance under any exponentially tilted law is at most the second moment about the midpoint of that interval.  Two integrations give \(K(\lambda)\leq\lambda^2d^2/8\).  Independence, exponential Markov, and optimization over \(\lambda>0\) therefore yield, for independent \(Z_i\in[0,1]\) and deterministic \(a_i\),
\[
 P\left(\left|\sum_i a_i\{Z_i-\mathbb EZ_i\}\right|>
 t\Bigl(\sum_i a_i^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\right)\leq2e^{-2t^2}. \tag{18}
\]
This derivation also applies conditionally when the weights and conditional means are fixed.

Apply (18) with equal weights to the first two sample blocks.  The definition \(t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}\) gives
\[
 P(E_0^c)\leq2e^{-2t_\alpha^2}=\frac{\alpha}{6J},
 \qquad
 P(E_{1x}^c)\leq2e^{-2t_\alpha^2}=\frac{\alpha}{6J}. \tag{19}
\]
On \(\Omega_x\), condition on \(\mathscr D_2=\sigma\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:iid-sampling} gives conditional independence.  Applying (18) to the weighted outcome residuals yields
\[
 P\left(\left.\left|\sum_iw_{ix}\{Y_i-\mu_x^P(A_i)\}\right|>
 t_\alpha\Bigl(\sum_iw_{ix}^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\,\right|\mathscr D_2\right)
 \leq\frac{\alpha}{6J}. \tag{20}
\]
By Lemma \texttt{lem:total-gram}, the weights reproduce every polynomial through degree \(\ell\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:holder-regression} consequently bounds the conditional bias by \(Lh^\beta\sum_i|w_{ix}|\).  Thus (20) proves \(P(E_{2x}^c)\leq\alpha/(6J)\).  A union bound and fixed finiteness of \(J\) give
\[
 P\left(E_0\cap\bigcap_{x\in\mathcal X}(E_{1x}\cap E_{2x})\right)
 \geq1-\frac{(2J+1)\alpha}{6J}\geq1-\alpha. \tag{21}
\]

On the event in (21), projection onto \([0,1]\) cannot enlarge the local regression error.  On \(\Omega_x\), \(b_x\leq\widehat b_x+b_1\) and hence
\[
 |\widehat b_x\widetilde\mu_x-b_x\mu_x^P(\delta)|
 \leq b_1+(\widehat b_x+b_1)B_x=D_x. \tag{22}
\]
On \(\Omega_x^c\), the two products lie in \([0,\widehat b_x]\) and \([0,b_x]\), respectively, so
\[
 |\widehat b_x\widetilde\mu_x-b_x\mu_x^P(\delta)|
 \leq\max\{\widehat b_x,b_x\}\leq\widehat b_x+b_1=D_x. \tag{23}
\]
Combining (22)--(23) with \(E_0\), then using contraction of the final projection about \(\theta_\delta(P)\in[0,1]\), gives
\[
 |\widehat\theta_n-\theta_\delta(P)|\leq b_0+\sum_xD_x. \tag{24}
\]
By Definition \texttt{def:honest-interval}, (24) is precisely the event \(\theta_\delta(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_n\).  Equation (21) proves the asserted uniform finite-sample coverage.

It remains to integrate the radius, including singular-Gram realizations.  The binomial calculation (4)--(5) in the proof of Theorem \texttt{thm:minimax-risk}, Lemma \texttt{lem:total-gram}, and Lemma \texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases} imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[B_x\mathbf 1\{\Omega_x\}]
 &\leq Lh^\beta\mathbb E_P\!\left[\sum_i|w_{ix}|\mathbf 1\{\Omega_x\}\right]
 +t_\alpha\mathbb E_P\!\left[\Bigl(\sum_iw_{ix}^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\mathbf 1\{\Omega_x\}\right]\\
 &\leq Ch^\beta+C\mathbb E_P[N_x^{-1/2}\mathbf 1\{N_x>0\}]
 \leq Ch^\beta. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{25}
\]
The split makes \(\widehat b_x\) independent of \((B_x,\Omega_x)\), and \(\mathbb E_P\widehat b_x=b_x\).  The two branches in Definition \texttt{def:honest-interval} therefore give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_PD_x
 &\leq(b_x+b_1)\mathbb E_P[B_x\mathbf 1\{\Omega_x\}]+b_1
 +(b_x+b_1)P(\Omega_x^c)\\
 &\leq C\{n^{-1/2}+b_xh^\beta\}
 \leq C\{n^{-1/2}+\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta\}. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{26}
\]
For the second line, Proposition \texttt{prop:pushforward-setup} gives \(b_x\leq C\delta^{\kappa+1}\), while Lemmas \texttt{lem:total-gram} and \texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases} give
\[
 P(\Omega_x^c)\leq Ce^{-cnh(\delta+h)^\kappa}
 \leq Ce^{-ch^{-2\beta}}\leq Ch^\beta. \tag{27}
\]
The terms containing \(b_1\) are \(O(n^{-1/2})\), since \(h\leq1\).  Intersecting with \([0,1]\) cannot increase length.  Thus (26), fixed \(J\), and \(b_0=O(n^{-1/2})\) yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)]
 \leq2b_0+2\sum_x\mathbb E_PD_x\leq Cr_n. \tag{28}
\]

For the converse, use the global and localized same-class pairs explicitly constructed in Theorem \texttt{thm:minimax-risk}.  Decrease their fixed amplitudes, if necessary, so that their product-law total variation is at most a constant \(\eta<1-2\alpha\); equations (9), (12), and (14) of that proof permit this without changing either separation order.  For either pair, let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be the product laws and let their target values have separation \(\Delta\).  Uniform coverage of an arbitrary interval \(C_n\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_0\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in C_n\}
 &\geq Q_0\{\theta_0\in C_n\}+Q_0\{\theta_1\in C_n\}-1\\
 &\geq(1-\alpha)+(1-\alpha-\eta)-1
 =1-2\alpha-\eta>0. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{29}
\]
On this event an interval has length at least \(\Delta\), whence
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{len}(C_n)]
 \geq\Delta(1-2\alpha-\eta). \tag{30}
\]
The global pair has \(\Delta\asymp n^{-1/2}\), and the localized pair has \(\Delta\geq c\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta\).  Maximizing the two applications of (30) and using \(\max(u,v)\geq(u+v)/2\) proves \(L_n^\star\geq cr_n\).  Together, (21), (28), and (30) prove uniform honesty, the achieved expected length, and its minimax lower bound.

statements.statement: The phase boundary satisfies \(\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}/\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}\to\infty\). If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to0\), then \(r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\) (regular regime). If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to c\in(0,\infty)\), both summands of \(r_n\) have order \(n^{-1/2}\) (critical regime). If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to\infty\) and \(\delta_n\to0\), then \(r_n\asymp\delta_n^{\kappa+1}(n\delta_n^\kappa)^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\) (atom-dominated regime). If \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), then \(r_n\asymp n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\) (fixed-threshold regime). At \(\delta_n=0\), \(q_x(0)=0\), \(\theta_0(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y]\), and the construction reduces to bounded-mean inference at rate \(n^{-1/2}\).
statements.justification: The phase diagram states when the published root-\(n\) paradigm is valid, critical, or false for the exact clamp.
statements.gap: Existing LMTP theory separates pathwise differentiable policies from excluded threshold policies but supplies no quantitative boundary between regular and atom-dominated sequences.
statements.consumer: The four regimes tell an applied user whether a threshold choice supports ordinary precision, requires the bias-aware atom interval, or behaves like a fixed nonparametric point target.
statements.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 D=\beta\kappa+2\beta+\kappa+1,
 \qquad e_n=\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n},
 \qquad c_n=\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}.
\]
By the definitions of the two scales,
\[
 \frac{c_n}{e_n}
 =n^{1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)-1/(2D)}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
because
\[
 2D-(2\beta+\kappa+1)=2\beta\kappa+2\beta+\kappa+1>0.
\]

Write \(T_n=\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\) for the atom term in \(r_n\).  On every subsequence on which \(\delta_n/e_n\to\infty\), Lemma \(\texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases}\) gives
\[
 h_n\asymp(n\delta_n^\kappa)^{-1/(2\beta+1)}
\]
and hence
\[
 T_n\asymp
 n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}
 \delta_n^{D/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
Since \(c_n^D=n^{-1/2}\), this identity also yields
\[
 \frac{T_n}{n^{-1/2}}
 \asymp
 \left(\frac{\delta_n}{c_n}\right)^{D/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
On every subsequence on which \(\delta_n/e_n=O(1)\), the other conclusion of Lemma \(\texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases}\) gives \(h_n\asymp e_n\), and therefore
\[
 T_n\leq C e_n^{\beta+\kappa+1}
 =C n^{-(\beta+\kappa+1)/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}
 =o(n^{-1/2}),
\]
where the last relation follows from
\[
 \frac{\beta+\kappa+1}{2\beta+\kappa+1}-\frac12
 =\frac{\kappa+1}{2(2\beta+\kappa+1)}>0.
\]

Suppose first that \(\delta_n/c_n\to0\).  Every subsequence has a further subsequence on which \(\delta_n/e_n\) is bounded or tends to infinity.  The preceding two displays show on either such further subsequence that \(T_n=o(n^{-1/2})\).  The subsequence criterion for convergence therefore gives \(T_n=o(n^{-1/2})\) on the original sequence, so Definition \(\texttt{def:frontier}\) implies \(r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\).

If \(\delta_n/c_n\to c\in(0,\infty)\), then \(c_n/e_n\to\infty\) implies \(\delta_n/e_n\to\infty\), and the displayed ratio for \(T_n\) is bounded above and away from zero.  Thus both summands of \(r_n\) have order \(n^{-1/2}\).  If \(\delta_n/c_n\to\infty\) and \(\delta_n\to0\), then again \(\delta_n/e_n\to\infty\), while the same ratio tends to infinity.  Consequently the atom term dominates and
\[
 r_n\asymp T_n
 \asymp\delta_n^{\kappa+1}(n\delta_n^\kappa)^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
If \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), then \(\delta_n/e_n\to\infty\), so Lemma \(\texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases}\) yields \(h_n\asymp n^{-1/(2\beta+1)}\).  Because \(\delta_n^{\kappa+1}\) is then bounded above and away from zero and \(\beta/(2\beta+1)<1/2\),
\[
 r_n\asymp n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
Theorem \(\texttt{thm:minimax-risk}\) and Theorem \(\texttt{thm:honest-length}\) transfer these comparisons of \(r_n\) to minimax absolute risk and minimax honest expected length, respectively.

It remains to verify the endpoint \(\delta_n=0\).  Proposition \(\texttt{prop:pushforward-setup}\) gives \(q_x(0)=0\) for every stratum.  Its pushforward formula at zero, together with \(d_0(A)=A\), also gives \(P(A=0\mid X=x)=0\); summing over the finitely many strata gives \(P(A=0)=0\).  The definition of the observed-data target therefore gives
\[
 \theta_0(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>0\}]=\mathbb E_PY.
\]
In Definition \(\texttt{def:total-gram-estimator}\), \(\widehat b_x=0\) for every \(x\) almost surely, and \(\widehat\nu_n\) is the sample mean of the bounded outcomes on \(I_0\).  Thus the estimator center is exactly that bounded sample mean.  Finally, Definition \(\texttt{def:frontier}\) gives \(r_n=n^{-1/2}\) at \(\delta_n=0\), and the already established coverage and expected-length bounds in Theorem \(\texttt{thm:honest-length}\) show directly, without any extraneous equation reference, that the accompanying construction is honest bounded-mean inference of root-\(n\) order.  This proves every asserted regime.

statements.statement: In the one-stratum model with \(\beta=\kappa=1\) and \(\pi(a)=2a\), whenever \(\delta_n\gg n^{-1/4}\), \(h_n\asymp(n\delta_n)^{-1/3}\), the localized Bernoulli alternatives have product Kullback--Leibler divergence of order \(n\delta_n h_n^3\), and their target separation is of order \(\delta_n^2h_n\). The regular-to-atom transition is exactly \(\delta_n\asymp n^{-1/10}\).
statements.justification: This explicit calibration is the requested early-kill test and checks the general exponents against a transparent design.
statements.gap: No cited LMTP or degenerate-design result computes this atom-attenuated transition for the deterministic clamp mean.
statements.consumer: The calibration supplies a simulation benchmark and a unit test for an implementation of the proposed interval.
statements.proof_tex:
Here \(\beta=\kappa=1\), and therefore the definitions give
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}=n^{-1/4},
 \qquad
 \delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}
 =n^{-1/[2(1+2+1+1)]}=n^{-1/10}.
\]
If \(\delta_n\gg n^{-1/4}\), Lemma \(\texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases}\) gives
\[
 h_n\asymp(n\delta_n)^{-1/3}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{h_n}{\delta_n}
 \asymp(n\delta_n^4)^{-1/3}\longrightarrow0.
\]

We now make the localized Bernoulli bump construction invoked in Theorem \(\texttt{thm:minimax-risk}\) explicit.  Let \(K(u)=(1-|u|)_+\), choose a fixed \(0<\eta\leq\min\{L,1/4\}\), and set
\[
 g_n(a)=\eta h_nK\left(\frac{a-\delta_n}{h_n}\right).
\]
Let \(P_0\) and \(P_1\) have \(X=1\) almost surely, the common conditional treatment density \(\pi(a)=2a\), and conditional outcome laws
\[
 Y\mid A=a\sim\operatorname{Ber}(1/2)
 \quad\text{under }P_0,
 \qquad
 Y\mid A=a\sim\operatorname{Ber}(1/2+g_n(a))
 \quad\text{under }P_1.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the support \([\delta_n-h_n,\delta_n+h_n]\) lies in \([0,1]\): the lower endpoint is positive because \(h_n/\delta_n\to0\), and the upper endpoint is below one because \(\delta_n\leq\bar\delta<1\) and \(h_n\to0\).  Both regressions take values in \([0,1]\).  The function \(g_n\) is \(\eta\)-Lipschitz, so the two regressions satisfy Assumption \(\texttt{ass:holder-regression}\) for \(\beta=1\) with radius \(L\).  The density \(\pi(a)=2a\) integrates to one, satisfies Assumption \(\texttt{ass:conditional-density-law}\), and satisfies Assumption \(\texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning}\) for \(\kappa=1\), because the declared ranges give \(c_-\leq2\leq c_+\).  The one-cell mass is one and hence satisfies Assumption \(\texttt{ass:stratum-mass}\).  Thus Definition \(\texttt{def:model-class}\) shows that \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal M\); in particular, these are same-class alternatives.

For \(0\leq g\leq1/4\), define
\[
 f(g)=\operatorname{KL}\{\operatorname{Ber}(1/2+g),\operatorname{Ber}(1/2)\}.
\]
Direct differentiation gives \(f(0)=f'(0)=0\) and
\[
 f''(g)=\frac{1}{(1/2+g)(1/2-g)}.
\]
This second derivative is bounded above and away from zero on \([0,1/4]\).  The identity
\[
 f(g)=\int_0^g(g-t)f''(t)\,\mathrm dt
\]
therefore gives constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), independent of \(g\), such that
\[
 c g^2\leq
 \operatorname{KL}\{\operatorname{Ber}(1/2+g),\operatorname{Ber}(1/2)\}
 \leq Cg^2.
\]
The two laws have the same treatment margin.  Since \(a\asymp\delta_n\) uniformly on the support of \(g_n\), conditioning on \(A\) and changing variables \(u=(a-\delta_n)/h_n\) show that the one-observation divergence satisfies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)
 &\asymp \int_0^1 2a\,g_n(a)^2\,\mathrm da \\
 &\asymp \delta_n h_n^3
 \int_{-1}^1K(u)^2\,\mathrm du
 \asymp\delta_nh_n^3.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:iid-sampling}\) makes the product log-likelihood ratio the sum of its \(n\) one-observation counterparts.  Taking expectation, equivalently using the product-divergence calculation in the localized lower bound of Theorem \(\texttt{thm:minimax-risk}\), therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_1^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 =n\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)
 \asymp n\delta_nh_n^3.
\]
The bandwidth relation makes this quantity of constant order.

For the target separation, the definition of \(\theta_{\delta_n}\), together with \(\pi(a)=2a\), gives
\[
 q(\delta_n)=\int_0^{\delta_n}2a\,\mathrm da=\delta_n^2
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_{\delta_n}(P_1)-\theta_{\delta_n}(P_0)
 &=q(\delta_n)g_n(\delta_n)
   +\int_{\delta_n}^1 2a\,g_n(a)\,\mathrm da \\
 &=\eta\delta_n^2h_n+O(\delta_nh_n^2).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Both displayed contributions are nonnegative, and \(h_n/\delta_n\to0\); hence the separation is \(\asymp\delta_n^2h_n\).  This is the explicit localized bump construction used by the minimax lower bound, so the reference is unambiguous.

Finally, equating the atom separation with the root-\(n\) term and substituting the bandwidth order gives
\[
 \delta_n^2(n\delta_n)^{-1/3}=n^{-1/2}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \delta_n^{5/3}=n^{-1/6}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \delta_n=n^{-1/10}.
\]
This is exactly the transition asserted in Theorem \(\texttt{thm:phase-diagram}\).

statements.statement:
Specialize the declared parameter to \(\beta=1\), so that \(\ell=0\), and take \(\delta_n\equiv0\).  For the realized design \(Z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), define
\[
Q_{n,x}(z)=\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha),
\qquad
\rho_n(z)=\max_{x\in\mathcal X}Q_{n,x}(z).
\]
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), the maps \(Q_{n,x}\) and \(\rho_n\) are Borel measurable, hence almost everywhere strongly measurable and integrable under the \(n\)-fold observed-design law, with
\[
0\leq Q_{n,x}(z)\leq Lh_n+t_\alpha,
\qquad
0\leq\rho_n(z)\leq Lh_n+t_\alpha.
\]
Consequently every literal real integral \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\) in this specialization is well defined, and the set of integrated handles whose real supremum defines \(\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)\) is nonempty and bounded above.  There are \(P_0\in\mathcal M\), \(x_0\in\mathcal X\), and constants \(c_0>0\) and \(C<\infty\), depending only on the declared constants, such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
h_n=n^{-1/(\kappa+3)},
\qquad
\mathbb E_{P_0}\rho_n(Z)\geq
\mathbb E_{P_0}Q_{n,x_0}(Z)\geq c_0h_n,
\qquad
\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)\geq c_0h_n.
\]
Since \(r_n=n^{-1/2}\) in this specialization,
\[
\frac{2\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)}{r_n}
\geq2c_0n^{(\kappa+1)/(2(\kappa+3))}\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad
\frac{L_n^\star}{r_n}\leq C.
\]
The worst-case expected full length of an untruncated symmetric interval with realized radius \(\rho_n\) has the same divergent lower-order comparison.  Thus the literal zero-totalized real-integral candidate cannot furnish a single sharp asymptotic minimax-constant theorem uniformly over the full declared \(\beta\)-range and all threshold regimes.  This result does not decide marginal honesty, sharpness for any separately fixed \(\beta>1\), or the general exact minimax constant.
statements.proof_tex:
Set \(\beta=1\).  The declared convention for integer smoothness gives \(\ell=\beta-1=0\).  Set \(\delta_n=0\), and abbreviate \(t=t_\alpha\).  The symbol declarations \(J\geq1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\) imply \(12J/\alpha>1\), so \(t>0\).

We first prove the measurability and integrability assertions for the literal realized objective.  Fix \(n\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and a nonempty active index set \(S\subseteq I_2\), of cardinality \(s\).  On the event \(S_{z,x}=S\), write \(a=(A_i)_{i\in S}\).  By \(\text{def:exact-modulus-handle}\), degree-zero feasibility is exactly
\[
\sum_{i\in S}w_i=1,
\tag{1}
\]
with all coordinates outside \(S\) equal to zero.  Let \(\mathcal H_{1,L}\) denote the class in that definition and put
\[
B_S(a,w)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{1,L}}
\left|\sum_{i\in S}w_i f(a_i)-f(0)\right|.
\tag{2}
\]
The class \(\mathcal H_{1,L}\) is nonempty because it contains every constant function.  Its members take values in \([0,1]\) and, because \(\ell=0\), satisfy \(|f(a)-f(a')|\leq L|a-a'|\).  Hence, for any \(a,a'\) and \(w,w'\), the elementary inequalities \(|\sup_f u_f-\sup_f v_f|\leq\sup_f|u_f-v_f|\) and \(||u|-|v||\leq|u-v|\) give
\[
\left|B_S(a,w)-B_S(a',w')\right|
\leq \sum_{i\in S}|w_i-w_i'|
+L\sum_{i\in S}|w_i'|\,|a_i-a_i'|.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus \((a,w)\mapsto B_S(a,w)\) is continuous.

For the uniform feasible vector \(\bar w_i=1/s\), every active \(a_i\) lies in \([0,h_n]\), and therefore
\[
B_S(a,\bar w)
=\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{1,L}}
\left|\frac1s\sum_{i\in S}\{f(a_i)-f(0)\}\right|
\leq\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{1,L}}
\frac1s\sum_{i\in S}|f(a_i)-f(0)|
\leq Lh_n.
\tag{4}
\]
Also \(\|\bar w\|_2=s^{-1/2}\).  It follows that the infimum defining \(Q_{n,x}(z)\) is at most \(Lh_n+t/\sqrt{s}\leq L+t\).  Choose \(R=2+L/t\).  Since \(B_S\geq0\), every feasible \(w\) with \(\|w\|_2>R\) has objective larger than \(tR=L+2t>L+t\).  Therefore the defining infimum is unchanged when restricted to the nonempty compact set
\[
K_S=\left\{w\in\mathbb R^S:\sum_{i\in S}w_i=1, \|w\|_2\leq R\right\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Equation (3), uniformly over \(w\in K_S\), now implies that
\[
a\longmapsto
q_S(a):=\inf_{w\in K_S}\{B_S(a,w)+t\|w\|_2\}
\tag{6}
\]
is continuous.  Indeed,
\[
|q_S(a)-q_S(a')|
\leq LR\sqrt{s}\,\max_{i\in S}|a_i-a_i'|.
\tag{7}
\]

There are only finitely many subsets \(S\subseteq I_2\).  Each event \(\{S_{z,x}=S\}\) is Borel because it is specified by the discrete conditions \(X_i=x\) and the interval conditions \(0\leq A_i\leq h_n\).  On a nonempty such event, \(Q_{n,x}(z)=q_S((A_i)_{i\in S})\); on \(S=\varnothing\), \(Q_{n,x}(z)=0\) by the explicit empty-feasible-set totalization in \(\text{def:exact-modulus-handle}\).  The finite piecewise-continuous representation proves that \(Q_{n,x}\) is Borel measurable.

Let \(N_x=|S_{z,x}|\).  If \(N_x\geq1\), (4) and the uniform weights give the upper bound below.  Conversely, every feasible \(w\) satisfies (1), so Cauchy--Schwarz and nonnegativity of the exact bias give
\[
1=\left|\sum_{i\in S_{z,x}}w_i\right|
\leq\sqrt{N_x}\,\|w\|_2,
\qquad
B_{S_{z,x}}(a,w)+t\|w\|_2\geq\frac{t}{\sqrt{N_x}}.
\tag{8}
\]
Taking the infimum and including the totalized case \(N_x=0\) yields the pointwise bounds
\[
\mathbf 1\{N_x\geq1\}\frac{t}{\sqrt{N_x}}
\leq Q_{n,x}(z)
\leq\mathbf 1\{N_x\geq1\}
\left(Lh_n+\frac{t}{\sqrt{N_x}}\right)
\leq Lh_n+t.
\tag{9}
\]
Because \(\mathcal X\) has the finite cardinality \(J\), \(\rho_n(z)=\max_xQ_{n,x}(z)\) is also Borel measurable and satisfies \(0\leq\rho_n\leq Lh_n+t\).  A real-valued Borel map has separable range and is almost everywhere strongly measurable under every probability law.  The uniform finite bound in (9) then gives
\[
\int |Q_{n,x}(z)|\,\mathrm dP_{X,A}^{\otimes n}(z)
\leq Lh_n+t<\infty,
\qquad
\int |\rho_n(z)|\,\mathrm dP_{X,A}^{\otimes n}(z)
\leq Lh_n+t<\infty.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus these are integrable in the literal real Bochner sense used by \(\text{def:exact-modulus-handle}\); in particular, the integral is not set to zero by the undefined-integral convention.

For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), (9)--(10) and monotonicity of the integral imply
\[
0\leq
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,0,1,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},0,h_n,t)
\leq Lh_n+t.
\tag{11}
\]
The set of handles in (11) is nonempty once a member of \(\mathcal M\) is exhibited, and (11) makes it bounded above.  Hence its literal real supremum exists and is at least each of its members.

We now exhibit such a member and obtain a positive lower bound.  Define \(P_0\) by
\[
P_0(X=x)=\frac1J\quad(x\in\mathcal X),
\qquad
\pi_x(a)=(\kappa+1)a^\kappa\quad(0\leq a\leq1),
\qquad
Y=\frac12\quad P_0\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{12}
\]
The density integrates to one because \(\int_0^1(\kappa+1)a^\kappa\,\mathrm da=1\).  The declared parameter ranges give \(c_-\leq\kappa+1\leq c_+\), so \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\) almost everywhere by \(\text{ass:polynomial-thinning}\).  Also \(1/J\geq p_{\min}\) by \(\text{ass:stratum-mass}\), and the constant conditional regression \(\mu_x^{P_0}=1/2\) has zero remainder and satisfies \(\text{ass:holder-regression}\).  The conditional law in (12) satisfies \(\text{ass:conditional-density-law}\) by construction.  Therefore \(P_0\in\mathcal M\) by \(\text{def:model-class}\).  This also proves the nonemptiness required after (11).

For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(n^{-1/(\kappa+3)}\leq1-\bar\delta\).  With \(\beta=1\) and \(\delta_n=0\), the set in \(\text{def:bandwidth}\) is then the interval whose left endpoint solves \(nh^{\kappa+3}=1\).  Consequently
\[
h_n=n^{-1/(\kappa+3)},
\qquad
nh_n^{\kappa+3}=1,
\qquad
nh_n^{\kappa+1}=h_n^{-2}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{13}
\]

Fix \(x_0\in\mathcal X\), let \(m_n=|I_2|\), and put \(N=N_{x_0}\).  By \(\text{ass:iid-sampling}\) and (12),
\[
N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m_n,p_n),
\qquad
p_n=P_0(X=x_0,0\leq A\leq h_n)=\frac{h_n^{\kappa+1}}J,
\qquad
\lambda_n:=\mathbb E_{P_0}N=\frac{m_nh_n^{\kappa+1}}J.
\tag{14}
\]
Since \(m_n\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\lambda_n\geq\frac{n h_n^{\kappa+1}}{5J}
=\frac{h_n^{-2}}{5J}\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad
\lambda_n\leq nh_n^{\kappa+1}=h_n^{-2}.
\tag{15}
\]
For \(E_n=\{1\leq N\leq2\lambda_n\}\), the binomial formula, \(1-u\leq e^{-u}\), and Markov's inequality give
\[
P_0(N=0)=(1-p_n)^{m_n}\leq e^{-\lambda_n},
\qquad
P_0(N>2\lambda_n)\leq\frac12,
\qquad
P_0(E_n)\geq\frac12-e^{-\lambda_n}\geq\frac13
\tag{16}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  On \(E_n\), the lower bound in (9) and the upper bound on \(\lambda_n\) in (15) yield
\[
Q_{n,x_0}(Z)
\geq\frac{t}{\sqrt{N}}
\geq\frac{t}{\sqrt{2\lambda_n}}
\geq\frac{t h_n}{\sqrt2}.
\tag{17}
\]
Integrability was proved in (10), so taking the ordinary expectation in (17), rather than an extended integral or an undefined real integral, is legitimate.  Equations (16)--(17) give
\[
\mathbb E_{P_0}Q_{n,x_0}(Z)
\geq\frac{t}{3\sqrt2}h_n.
\tag{18}
\]
Set \(c_0=t_\alpha/(3\sqrt2)>0\).  Since \(\rho_n\geq Q_{n,x_0}\), (18) proves the first asserted expectation bound.  Since the handle at \((P_0,x_0)\) is a member of the nonempty bounded-above set in (11), the defining property of its real supremum proves
\[
\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)\geq c_0h_n.
\tag{19}
\]

Finally, \(\kappa+1>0\), so \(\delta_n^{\kappa+1}=0\).  Thus \(\text{def:frontier}\) gives \(r_n=n^{-1/2}\), and (13), (19) give
\[
\frac{2\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)}{r_n}
\geq2c_0n^{1/2-1/(\kappa+3)}
=2c_0n^{(\kappa+1)/(2(\kappa+3))}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{20}
\]
By \(\text{thm:honest-length}\), the displayed interval in that theorem is uniformly honest and has worst-case expected length at most \(Cr_n\).  Taking it as a candidate in the infimum defining \(L_n^\star\) gives \(L_n^\star/r_n\leq C\).  An untruncated symmetric interval with realized radius \(\rho_n\) has full length \(2\rho_n\), and (18) makes its worst-case expected length at least \(2c_0h_n\), whose ratio to \(r_n\) diverges by (20).  Because \(\beta=1\) and \(\delta_n=0\) are allowed, this single counterexample excludes a sharp theorem for this literal candidate that is uniform over the full declared smoothness range and every threshold regime.  Nothing in the argument proves or disproves marginal honesty, sharpness at a separately fixed \(\beta>1\), or the general exact minimax constant.

statements.statement:
There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the declared model constants, such that for every deterministic threshold sequence and all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c r_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
 \leq\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
 \mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}|\widehat\theta_n-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})|
 \leq C r_n.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}
 \{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in\mathrm{CI}_n\}\geq1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
 \mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)]\leq Cr_n,
\]
and every uniformly \((1-\alpha)\)-honest observed-sample interval over \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) has worst-case expected length at least \(cr_n\).  Thus \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\asymp L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\asymp r_n\), attained by the same total-Gram estimator and bias-aware interval as in the observed-data experiment.

statements.statement:
Let \(S\) and \(T\) be standard Borel spaces and let \((Z,W)\) be an \(S\times T\)-valued random element.  There is a Borel probability kernel \(K:S\times\mathcal B(T)\to[0,1]\) such that, writing \(P_Z\) for the law of \(Z\),
\[
 \Pr\{Z\in B,W\in C\}=\int_B K(z,C)\,P_Z(\mathrm dz)
\]
for every Borel \(B\subseteq S\) and \(C\subseteq T\).

source.verbatim_statement: Let X be a standard Borel space, Y a measurable space, and X and Y corresponding random variables. Then there exists a kernel μ from Y to X satisfying P(X ∈ B | Y) = μ(Y,B) for Borel B, and this kernel is unique almost surely with respect to the law of Y.
